lessons.name: Out-of-order CPU pipeline
lessons.role: Finds ready independent instructions while preserving architectural results.
lessons.description: A CPU often runs code whose next action depends on a branch, pointer or recently loaded value. An out-of-order core searches a window of decoded work for instructions whose inputs are ready. Register renaming separates accidental name reuse from real data dependencies, while a retirement mechanism makes completed work visible in the required order. Prediction can keep the window supplied but wrong predictions waste work. Arm Neoverse V2 provides a public example of rename and issue structures. This organization explains CPU strength in control-heavy services without claiming that every CPU or every workload benefits equally.

specs.context: A long dependent chain can remain slow despite multiple execution units.

interfaces.name: Architectural state

lessons.tradeoff: Larger windows and prediction structures discover more parallelism but consume area and power; dependent pointer chasing still exposes memory latency.

lessons.name: Scalar, vector and CPU matrix units
lessons.shortName: Scalar, vector and CPU matrix units
lessons.role: Executes different shapes of arithmetic within a general-purpose processor.
lessons.description: A scalar instruction updates one value; a vector instruction applies an operation across lanes; a matrix instruction consumes a tile containing many values. These are execution resources inside a CPU, not mutually exclusive kinds of computer. Intel AMX exposes tile storage and tile matrix multiplication, while Arm SVE lets software express vector work with predicates and a vector-length-aware model. Loads, address calculation and branches still surround the arithmetic. Efficient code arranges contiguous data, handles tails and chooses supported types so that wider arithmetic produces useful results instead of multiplying padding or waiting for operands.

specs.label: Arithmetic type

lessons.tradeoff: Wider units increase arithmetic throughput but raise operand demand and can leave lanes idle on short or irregular arrays.
lessons.whyAI: CPU vector and matrix capabilities can accelerate preprocessing, embedding reductions and smaller inference batches while preserving general-purpose control.

lessons.name: Cache coherence and NUMA placement
lessons.role: Keeps shared cache lines consistent while preserving awareness of physical memory location.
lessons.description: Multiple CPU cores can cache copies of the same memory line. A coherence protocol tracks copies and coordinates ownership when a core writes. Coherence provides an agreement about values; it does not make every access equally close or eliminate software synchronization. In a NUMA system, memory controllers belong to different locality domains, so an address may be directly attached to one CPU and reached over a link from another. Thread placement and allocation policy determine which path dominates. The Linux kernel documents this distinction and exposes memory policy controls for local, bound and interleaved allocation.

specs.label: Coherence granularity
specs.context: Independent variables can still share one coherence unit.

specs.label: NUMA latency
specs.context: Nanoseconds depend on machine topology and contention; no universal ratio.

lessons.name: SIMT execution and divergent branches
lessons.role: Shares instruction issue across threads while tracking which lanes participate.
lessons.description: A GPU kernel describes many threads, but execution resources issue instructions to groups of threads. Threads can have different addresses and control decisions; the machine uses active masks to determine which lanes participate in a particular instruction. When a group takes different branches, the paths may require separate masked execution. Coalescing is a different concern: neighboring addresses can be combined into efficient memory transactions even when the arithmetic is identical. NVIDIA warps and AMD wavefronts instantiate related ideas with generation-specific details. The useful comparison follows the same small operation through these groups, counting both idle lanes and transferred bytes.

specs.label: Active-lane fraction
specs.context: A dimensionless instruction-level metric, distinct from chip utilization.

specs.label: Transaction efficiency
specs.context: Depends on address alignment, access size and memory behavior.

interfaces.signal: Masked instructions and memory transactions

lessons.tradeoff: Grouping similar requests can reduce divergence and scattered accesses, but rearranging them costs time and can increase request latency.

options: Memory transaction inefficiency

check.explanation: Uniform control can still generate many memory transactions when the addresses do not fall into shared transaction regions.

science.explanation: Count lane participation over issued instructions. The resulting fraction measures mask waste and has no time units.

lessons.name: Occupancy and asynchronous tile pipelines
lessons.role: Keeps work ready while controlling registers, scratchpad capacity and synchronization.
lessons.description: A GPU can switch to another ready execution group while one waits for data. Occupancy measures how many groups are resident relative to a hardware limit; it does not measure how many arithmetic units are doing useful work. Each block reserves registers and shared memory, so a large tile can improve reuse while reducing the number of resident blocks. An asynchronous pipeline instead overlaps loading a future tile with computing the current tile. Hopper’s Tensor Memory Accelerator is a disclosed data-movement example. Correct buffer ownership and completion barriers matter as much as the number of threads launched.

specs.label: Occupancy
specs.context: A resource-residency ratio, not FLOPS utilization.

specs.label: Double buffering
specs.context: Consumes additional scratchpad and needs explicit producer/consumer ordering.

science.explanation: Both terms are seconds per tile. Independent engines can overlap their work after pipeline fill; the slower stage sets the steady-state bound.

lessons.name: GPU chiplets and memory locality
lessons.role: Partitions compute and I/O physically while presenting a programmable accelerator.
lessons.description: Breaking an accelerator into chiplets changes where data must travel. In AMD’s MI300 family, compute chiplets connect through I/O dies and a package-level fabric to memory. MI300X is a GPU accelerator, whereas MI300A combines CPU and GPU compute with shared HBM in an APU package. A software-visible address space can hide the physical route without making its bandwidth or contention disappear. Chiplets can place different circuit functions on suitable processes and reuse design blocks, but introduce additional interfaces, test requirements and package assembly dependencies. A package diagram therefore needs both physical boundaries and logical memory connections.

lessons.name: Systolic arrays and tensor dataflow
lessons.role: Reuses operands through a regular network of multiply–accumulate elements.
lessons.description: A systolic array moves operands rhythmically between neighboring processing elements. Instead of repeatedly fetching every pair from a distant memory, each value contributes to several multiply–accumulate operations as it crosses the array. A dataflow choice determines whether weights, inputs or partial sums remain stationary for a tile. Filling and draining the array creates overhead, especially for small or awkward matrix shapes. Google’s original TPU is a disclosed matrix-engine example; TPU v4 adds system and embedding support. The array is only part of the machine: nonlinear operations, sparse lookups, compiler scheduling and communication still require other resources.

specs.value: One multiply plus one add = two operations
specs.context: Use this convention only when explicitly comparing compatible arithmetic.

specs.label: Tile utilization
specs.context: Shape padding and fill/drain cycles reduce realized throughput.

A recommendation lookup and a long-context language-model decode have different working sets and reuse, so comparing them solely by nominal operations per second hides the design rationale.

lessons.shortName: FPGA fabrics, DSP blocks and adaptive pipelines
lessons.role: Configures a spatial datapath around a stream and its timing constraints.
lessons.description: An FPGA uses configurable logic and routing to implement a circuit after manufacturing. A bitstream determines connections and state machines; it is different from launching threads on a fixed GPU datapath. Hardened DSP blocks provide arithmetic, embedded memories provide buffering, and processors may handle control. AMD Versal adds instruction-programmed AI Engines alongside programmable logic and DSP engines, so an AI Engine is not simply another name for FPGA fabric. Streaming sensor or packet pipelines can exploit this mixture, especially when custom interfaces or predictable latency matter. Mapping the design still requires timing closure and a complete path from input to output.

Finish every input without buffering

lessons.name: DPU and infrastructure offload
lessons.role: Moves selected networking and infrastructure work away from the host CPU.
lessons.description: A data processing unit usually combines a network interface, programmable processor resources and dedicated offload engines. Its purpose is often to handle infrastructure work such as packet steering, virtualization or storage access near the network path. NVIDIA’s BlueField documentation distinguishes DPU mode, where the embedded Arm subsystem owns NIC resources, from NIC mode. The phrase IPU can mean infrastructure processing unit in this context, but other vendors use the same initials differently. Offload improves an AI system only if it removes a measured bottleneck without creating excessive transfer, synchronization or control-plane overhead.

specs.context: Ownership and trust differ by operating mode.

specs.label: Service rate
specs.context: Bit rate alone omits per-packet work and protocol overhead.

interfaces.signal: Packets, descriptors and flow metadata

interfaces.name: Host or accelerator path
interfaces.signal: Steered data and completion notifications

lessons.tradeoff: Offload can free host cores and isolate infrastructure control, while adding software lifecycle, debugging and resource-allocation responsibilities.
lessons.whyAI: AI training needs predictable data and collective delivery; inference services also need networking and storage work beyond matrix multiplication.

Offload guarantees tenfold speedup
Network bandwidth becomes infinite

lessons.name: Wafer-scale compute and distributed SRAM
lessons.role: Keeps a very large compute fabric connected across a wafer-scale implementation.
lessons.description: A wafer-scale processor uses a connected area much larger than a conventional reticle-sized logic die. Cerebras WSE-3 provides a public example with many compute elements and distributed on-chip SRAM, integrated into a purpose-built system. The attraction is fine-grained local communication and a large aggregate memory fabric. It also demands mechanisms for defect tolerance, routing around unavailable resources, power delivery and heat removal. A wafer-scale drawing should retain these constraints instead of presenting one unlimited memory. Large models may still need external state movement or system-level streaming, so aggregate local SRAM bandwidth cannot be substituted for external memory bandwidth.

specs.label: Bandwidth scope

interfaces.signal: Weights, activations and routed messages

interfaces.name: System interfaces
interfaces.signal: Model state exchange and completed tensor results

lessons.tradeoff: Keeping communication local can reduce repeated off-chip movement, but the system must handle defects, thermal density and workloads that exceed local state capacity.
lessons.whyAI: Model partitions can exploit a large connected fabric if the compiler balances compute, SRAM and routing rather than merely filling every processing element.

Use redundant resources and a supported routing map so manufacturing defects do not require every region to be perfect.
Route intermediate activations through the fabric while keeping reusable state close to its consumer.
Schedule external transfers for state that cannot remain in distributed local SRAM.
Close power, cooling and system I/O budgets before treating the connected wafer as deployable capacity.
lessons.misconception: A wafer-scale chip is not one uniformly accessible giant register, and aggregate on-chip bandwidth is not equivalent to HBM bandwidth at a package boundary.

All local links form one external port
Bandwidth and capacity are the same unit

lessons.name: Analog and photonic arithmetic research
lessons.role: Explores physical multiply accumulation with explicit conversion and accuracy limits.
lessons.description: In analog in-memory computing, stored conductance can encode a weight and an applied voltage can encode an input. Currents combine to form a multiply–accumulate result that must be sensed and often digitized. IBM has demonstrated mixed-signal phase-change-memory research chips using this principle. Photonic tensor-core research instead encodes and combines signals using optical components, with electronic interfaces still required around the computation. Both approaches can reduce certain data movements or exploit physical parallelism, but noise, drift, calibration, conversion and unsupported operations determine complete-system usefulness. Research demonstrations establish a mechanism and measured experiment, not automatic production readiness for large AI services.

specs.label: Evidence status
specs.context: Laboratory arithmetic is separate from a qualified deployed service.

specs.label: Accounting boundary
specs.value: Array plus converters, control and memory
specs.context: Laser or conversion energy must be counted where the architecture requires it.

interfaces.name: Encoded inputs and weights
interfaces.signal: Voltages/conductances or optical signals

interfaces.name: Readout and digital control
interfaces.signal: Digitized results, calibration feedback and subsequent operations

lessons.tradeoff: Physical parallelism may reduce core arithmetic energy, while precision restoration, calibration and data conversion can consume much of the apparent benefit.
lessons.whyAI: Inference tolerance to numerical error creates opportunities, but model quality and full operator coverage must survive real device variations.

mechanism: Choose how numerical values are represented by conductance, voltage or an optical signal.
Program weights and calibrate the physical response, including device variation and drift.
Perform the physical combination that approximates the desired matrix operation.
Sense and convert the result, accounting for noise and the precision required by the next stage.
Evaluate model quality and total energy including peripherals, communication and operations performed outside the analog or optical core.
lessons.misconception: Light does not make data movement or heat disappear, and an analog multiply–accumulate does not supply arbitrary exact digital arithmetic.

check.question: What belongs in a fair analog-versus-digital energy comparison?
options: Converters, control, memory traffic and achieved model quality
Only the crossbar’s current
Only the optical propagation time
check.explanation: The complete task needs interfaces and acceptable outputs; excluding them can turn a component result into an unsupported system claim.

lessons.learningObjective: Distinguish a physical arithmetic demonstration from a complete production accelerator claim.
lessons.engineeringExample: Synthetic error budget: if sensing and weight drift each consume part of a permissible error margin, a larger array may need recalibration or wider digital correction even when its core operation is fast.

lessons.name: Workload contract and architecture selection
lessons.role: Turns desired service behavior into measurable hardware and software requirements.
lessons.description: A custom-chip project begins by defining the work it must perform and the conditions under which success will be measured. A workload contract records operator shapes, numerical quality, latency targets, throughput, state capacity and expected model changes. Architecture exploration then asks how much arithmetic, memory, communication and control are needed together. Existing IP can supply processors, interfaces or other blocks, but its licensing and integration constraints matter. Meta’s MTIA co-design account is one public example of workload-driven development. A chip that excels on one benchmark can still fail the contract if the production graph falls back to a slow unsupported path.

specs.label: Acceptance unit
specs.context: For example accepted requests/s under a stated latency target.

specs.label: Requirements horizon
specs.value: Present mix plus explicit change scenarios
specs.context: Future operator needs are assumptions, not known measurements.

interfaces.name: Service and model teams
interfaces.signal: Representative traces and acceptance criteria

interfaces.name: Architecture and software teams
interfaces.signal: Resource budgets, supported operations and executable model prototypes

lessons.tradeoff: Specialization improves the frequent path while narrowing flexibility; programmable fallbacks and memory headroom cost area but can extend useful life.
lessons.whyAI: AI models evolve on a different schedule from silicon, so a workload contract must expose assumptions that may fail before a product ships.

mechanism: Collect production-like traces, including unusual sequence lengths, operator shapes and tail-latency cases.
Define acceptable numerical quality and measurement conditions so the performance target has a stable denominator.
Build resource models for arithmetic, memory traffic, resident state and inter-device communication.
Prototype the compiler and critical kernels against architectural alternatives before fixing the hardware interfaces.
Record unsupported paths and change scenarios, then use these as explicit risks in the architecture decision.
lessons.misconception: A chip specification is not just a target peak FLOPS number; it is a contract for complete workloads and their operating conditions.

check.question: Which requirement most directly prevents a misleading inference performance target?
options: A quality threshold and latency condition attached to throughput
The largest possible transistor count
A product name shared with a benchmark winner
check.explanation: Throughput is only useful when the outputs satisfy the task and arrive under the required service conditions.

science.explanation: λk is requests/s for workload class k and qk is bytes or operations per request. Dresource is bytes/s or operations/s.
science.assumptions: Linear aggregation before queueing and reuse effects; correlated bursts require an additional capacity margin.

lessons.engineeringExample: Synthetic mix: 80 requests/s needing 1 GB each and 20 needing 4 GB each creates 160 GB/s of un-reused traffic. Designing from the common 1 GB request alone underestimates the mix by a factor of two.

lessons.name: RTL and functional verification
lessons.role: Checks that a cycle-based design obeys its specification before manufacture.
lessons.description: Register-transfer level code describes how state changes and data moves between registers. Simulation executes that description under selected stimulus; assertions and formal methods test properties under stated assumptions. Coverage asks whether planned situations were exercised, not whether every possible bug has been excluded. An accelerator needs arithmetic checks as well as reset, backpressure, ordering, error and clock-domain behavior. OpenTitan supplies a public example of staged verification planning, reusable test environments and regression evidence. Verification must also cover integrated IP boundaries, because individually correct blocks can disagree about protocols or the meaning of a completed operation.

specs.label: Verification target
specs.context: Tests require an expected behavior independent of the implementation.

specs.label: Coverage
specs.context: Code or functional coverage is not a mathematical probability of correctness.

interfaces.name: Architecture specification
interfaces.signal: Cycle behavior, numerical rules and protocol contracts

interfaces.name: Verification evidence
interfaces.signal: Assertions, regression results, coverage and unresolved failures

lessons.tradeoff: Exhaustive state exploration grows rapidly; engineers combine abstraction, constrained stimulus, formal properties and targeted tests rather than trusting one technique.
lessons.whyAI: A rare deadlock or wrong accumulator rounding can corrupt long training runs even if the common matrix benchmark appears correct.

mechanism: Write a test plan from externally meaningful requirements, including illegal inputs and recovery behavior.
Construct reference models for arithmetic and protocol state that can detect implementation disagreement.
Drive simulation with directed corner cases and constrained randomized sequences.
Use assertions or formal checks for invariants such as no buffer overwrite before consumption.
Review failures and coverage gaps, then repeat regressions after integration changes and before stage approval.
lessons.misconception: Passing simulation does not prove all states correct; high coverage does not excuse a missing requirement or an invalid formal assumption.

check.question: What makes a test useful for a hardware handshake?
options: It checks behavior under backpressure and reset against a protocol rule
It repeats the RTL calculation verbatim
It only counts how often valid is high
check.explanation: A handshake’s correctness depends on timing and ownership under difficult conditions, not merely exercising signals.

science.explanation: b is the number of independent state bits and Nstates is a count. Even modest state creates a large space of possible configurations.

lessons.learningObjective: Explain how simulation, assertions, formal checks and coverage contribute different evidence.
lessons.engineeringExample: Synthetic FIFO property: after a valid item is accepted, it must emerge once in order unless reset explicitly cancels it. A test that pauses the consumer reveals bugs hidden by continuous ready signals.

lessons.name: PDKs, synthesis and physical closure
lessons.role: Converts logical behavior into a manufacturable layout under electrical constraints.
lessons.description: A process design kit connects circuit design to a fabrication process through device models, layer definitions, design rules and related technology files. Synthesis maps RTL into a cell library; placement and routing assign locations and wires. Extracted resistance and capacitance alter timing and power estimates, so a design that passed logic simulation may need changes after layout. Clock distribution, voltage drop and thermal conditions further constrain operation. OpenROAD provides a public sequence of digital implementation tools, while SKY130 provides an accessible PDK example. Those educational references do not disclose leading-edge foundry recipes or automatically qualify a design for production.

specs.value: Models and rules for a specific process
specs.context: A PDK is not the complete manufacturing recipe.

specs.label: Timing slack
specs.context: Positive setup slack alone does not establish hold, power or reliability closure.

Place cells, distribute clocks and route signals under the technology’s geometry rules.
Extract parasitics and analyze setup, hold, power integrity and other required corners.
Iterate architecture or implementation where constraints conflict, then check physical connectivity and rule compliance with the required signoff flow.

options: The actual interconnect parasitics were not yet represented accurately
RTL determines physical wire length
All logic gates have zero capacitance
check.explanation: Physical placement and routing introduce resistance and capacitance that affect signal delay beyond functional logic behavior.

science.explanation: All terms are seconds along a selected timing path; wire delay follows the extracted physical interconnect.
science.assumptions: Simplified setup-path model; real analysis includes clock skew, uncertainty, corners and separate hold checks.

lessons.engineeringExample: Synthetic path: a 1.0 ns requirement and 0.7 ns cell delay leave 0.3 ns for wires and margin. If extracted wiring adds 0.4 ns, the path misses by 0.1 ns before additional uncertainty.

lessons.name: Tapeout, bring-up and productization
lessons.role: Coordinates design release, manufacturing partners and software into a usable product.
lessons.description: Tapeout releases a defined physical design for mask preparation and manufacturing; it is a milestone, not proof that silicon works. Foundry fabrication, wafer screening, memory supply, package assembly and final test produce hardware that must still be brought up and qualified. A fabless company can own the design while relying on foundries, memory suppliers, substrate makers and assembly/test partners. Board and system integrators add power, cooling and interfaces, while software teams deliver firmware, drivers and executable support. The exact contracts vary. A reviewable ecosystem map therefore names responsibilities separately and marks announcement, first silicon, qualification and deployment as different states.

specs.context: States require different evidence and can include iterations.

specs.label: Partner roles
specs.context: One organization may perform several roles; labels are not proof of a specific partnership.

interfaces.name: Qualified system
interfaces.signal: Screened hardware, enabled software and acceptance evidence

lessons.whyAI: Useful AI capacity requires supported models and reliable system operation, so delivered silicon can remain unusable while firmware or qualification is incomplete.

A physical design release identifier
A chosen mask data set

science.explanation: The logical AND is true only when every required gate has supporting acceptance evidence. Gates are states, not percentages of nominal progress.

lessons.name: Custom-chip volume economics
lessons.role: Compares lifecycle costs per useful result under explicit volume and performance assumptions.
lessons.description: A custom accelerator can reduce recurring system cost while adding substantial development obligations. Non-recurring engineering includes design, verification, masks, software enablement and possible respins. Recurring cost includes usable silicon, memory, packaging, test, boards and operation. Chiplets can improve reuse or process choice, yet introduce links and package costs. The Chiplet Actuary research supplies a cost-model structure, not current commercial prices. The decisive denominator is useful delivered work over the product’s life. A lower chip purchase price can be overwhelmed by poor utilization, a shorter useful software lifetime or the need for more devices to satisfy the same service target.

specs.label: Fixed cost
specs.context: Amortize over delivered usable volume, with explicit accounting period.

specs.label: Variable cost
specs.context: Include screening and assembly losses consistently, avoiding repeated yield penalties.

interfaces.signal: NRE, volume, screened component costs and qualification assumptions

interfaces.name: Service economics
interfaces.signal: Lifecycle currency per useful result and break-even sensitivity

lessons.tradeoff: Specialization can lower cost at sufficient volume; uncertainty in demand, software portability and model evolution can prevent fixed costs from being recovered.
lessons.whyAI: Custom silicon is justified by sustained useful workload advantage, so software development and delivered utilization belong beside die and package costs.

It halves automatically

lessons.name: Full memory hierarchy and input path
lessons.shortName: Full memory hierarchy and input path
lessons.role: Tracks data through storage, host memory, accelerator memory, caches and operand storage.
lessons.description: A tensor does not jump directly from a dataset into an arithmetic unit. Persistent storage supplies files or objects; host memory holds decoded and prepared data; a transfer path places tensors in accelerator memory. Caches and software-managed SRAM then stage tiles close to execution, while registers hold immediate operands and accumulators. Results may return through the hierarchy or remain resident for later kernels. Each level has a different capacity, bandwidth, latency and ownership policy. The route is workload-specific: direct-storage paths can bypass some host copies, while coherent shared-memory systems alter ownership without eliminating the physical travel.

specs.label: Capacity
specs.context: Allocated, usable and physically installed memory can differ.

specs.label: Bandwidth and latency
specs.context: High bandwidth requires enough independent work; it does not imply low individual-access latency.

interfaces.name: Dataset or checkpoint storage
interfaces.signal: Persistent bytes decoded into tensors

interfaces.name: Registers and scratchpad
interfaces.signal: Operand tiles and partial sums consumed by arithmetic

lessons.tradeoff: Larger nearby storage improves reuse but costs area; offloading to a larger distant level increases transfer time and may expose a new bottleneck.
lessons.whyAI: Input starvation, HBM traffic, cache misses and register spilling occur on different links and require different remedies.

mechanism: Read persistent data and perform any required decompression, parsing and preprocessing in the supported input path.
Place prepared tensors in host or shared memory, tracking pinning, ownership and asynchronous transfer completion.
Move or map tensors into accelerator-accessible memory through the actual system interconnect.
Stage reusable tiles through caches or explicit SRAM and finally into registers or tensor operand storage.
Retain, evict or write back results according to their next consumer and lifetime, measuring traffic at each chosen boundary.
lessons.misconception: All memory bytes are not equally close, and a unified virtual address does not eliminate copies, migration or physical bandwidth limits.

check.question: A kernel’s register use causes spills. Where should diagnosis begin?
options: The compiler allocation and spill traffic path
Only the storage array’s capacity
The tokenizer’s vocabulary size
check.explanation: Spilling moves temporary state out of registers into a less local storage path, adding traffic even when the dataset input rate is adequate.

science.explanation: For level j, Qj is bytes crossing its boundary and Bj sustainable bytes/s. Tj is seconds of transfer demand.
science.assumptions: Overlap can hide some demand, but traffic must be counted at each boundary separately; cache reuse changes Qj.

lessons.name: Choosing SRAM, HBM, DDR, LPDDR or GDDR
lessons.shortName: Choosing SRAM, HBM, DDR, LPDDR or GDDR
lessons.role: Matches memory technology and package integration to a workload’s access pattern.
lessons.description: Memory alternatives solve different constraints. SRAM integrates near logic and supports fast local access, but has lower bit density than DRAM. HBM uses stacked DRAM and many short package connections. DDR commonly supplies expandable host memory; LPDDR emphasizes mobile-style power and signaling choices and also appears in some server and custom-accelerator designs. GDDR uses high-rate interfaces in discrete memory packages, providing another accelerator memory route. Capacity, sustained bandwidth, power, board area, package complexity and supply all matter. A valid comparison fixes a generation and configuration instead of treating one family as universally faster or cheaper.

specs.label: Interface bandwidth
specs.context: Bytes/s before utilization losses; effective data rate already accounts for signaling transfers.

specs.label: Technology choice
specs.context: Controller/PHY, package, board and cooling must support the chosen interface.

interfaces.name: Workload memory demand
interfaces.signal: Resident bytes, reuse, burst size and access concurrency

interfaces.name: Memory subsystem

Return and combine outputs, then measure total state, active arithmetic and communication as separate budgets.
lessons.misconception: Inactive parameters do not vanish from memory, and fewer active FLOPS do not guarantee proportionally lower token latency.

check.question: Why can an MoE model require large memory despite low active parameters per token?
options: All experts must remain stored or be fetched when selected
The router deletes inactive weights permanently
Active FLOPS and memory bytes are identical quantities
check.explanation: Conditional execution changes which expert weights participate in a token’s work; it does not eliminate the total model state.

science.title: Simple dispatch volume
science.equation: Qdispatch = T k d s fremote
science.explanation: T is tokens, k selected experts/token, d activation elements, s bytes/element and fremote the remote fraction. Q is bytes.
science.assumptions: Counts one-way activation payload only; return data, metadata, duplicates and protocol overhead are additional.

lessons.learningObjective: Separate MoE’s active computation savings from total state and routing costs.
lessons.engineeringExample: Synthetic dispatch: 1,000 tokens, two experts per token, 4,096-element activations, two bytes/element and half remote gives 8,192,000 remote payload bytes one way, before return outputs or metadata.
lessons.evidenceNotes: Routing policy and storage placement are model-specific. The toy traffic estimate does not describe any named production model or guarantee expert balance.

lessons.name: Parallelism as a memory and communication budget
lessons.shortName: Parallelism as a memory and communication budget
lessons.role: Chooses tensor, pipeline, data and state partitions under topology and dependency constraints.
lessons.description: Distributed execution divides work and state in several ways. Data parallelism processes different examples and synchronizes updates. Tensor parallelism splits operators and exchanges partial results. Pipeline parallelism assigns layer groups to stages, introducing activation transfers and possible bubbles. State sharding distributes parameters, gradients or optimizer state that would otherwise be replicated. These choices often combine. More devices increase available memory and arithmetic, but also add collectives, synchronization and topology constraints. A good plan places frequent exchanges on suitable links and measures how much communication is exposed on the critical path instead of assuming that all network time overlaps with computation.

specs.label: Partitioned object
specs.value: Examples, tensor dimensions, layers or persistent state
specs.context: Different partitions create different communication patterns.

specs.label: Collective cost
specs.context: Small messages can be latency-limited; large messages can be bandwidth-limited.

interfaces.name: Model and device topology
interfaces.signal: Tensor sizes, layer graph, state layout and link capacities

interfaces.name: Distributed step
interfaces.signal: Scheduled compute, collectives and synchronization

lessons.tradeoff: Sharding can make a model fit but increase traffic; larger parallel groups can reduce local work enough that communication dominates.
lessons.whyAI: Training and inference have different collective frequencies and batch shapes, so a partition that trains efficiently may serve poorly.

mechanism: Choose which dimensions of work and state need partitioning to meet local memory and time constraints.
Derive the transfers and collectives implied by each partition rather than starting from a chip count.
Map frequent communication onto topology regions with sufficient latency and bandwidth characteristics.
Schedule overlap only where producer and consumer dependencies allow it without premature buffer reuse.
Measure completed step or token latency and adjust partition size when smaller local compute no longer amortizes communication.

science.title: Communication approximation
science.explanation: n is latency-bearing phases, α seconds/phase, Q transferred bytes and Beff useful bytes/s for the chosen algorithm and topology.
science.assumptions: A coarse model; contention, overlap, reduction compute and protocol behavior can change both terms.

lessons.learningObjective: Derive communication consequences from a chosen partition and topology.
lessons.engineeringExample: Synthetic collective: four latency-bearing phases at 5 μs plus 100 MB at 50 GB/s gives about 2.02 ms. Cutting local compute to 1 ms exposes this cost unless a valid overlap schedule exists.
lessons.evidenceNotes: No particular collective algorithm is assumed universally. Published TPU topology and ZeRO methods provide examples, not interchangeable performance constants.

lessons.name: Prefill/decode disaggregation and useful serving rate
lessons.shortName: Prefill/decode disaggregation and useful serving rate
lessons.role: Separates workload phases when independent scheduling benefits exceed the state-transfer cost.
lessons.description: A serving system can run prefill and decode on different resource pools. Prefill produces KV state that must become accessible to the decode worker, creating a transfer and handoff boundary. Separating the phases may prevent long prompts from disrupting token-generation deadlines and allows different batching or hardware choices. It also adds network demand, queue coordination and failure cases. DistServe studies this design under explicit service objectives. PagedAttention addresses a different layer: efficient mapping and sharing of KV memory blocks. Combining allocation and scheduling methods requires measuring accepted requests that meet latency and quality targets, not just the largest raw token count.

specs.label: Goodput
specs.value: Accepted requests/s meeting stated service objectives
specs.context: Raw throughput includes outputs that may miss deadlines.

specs.label: Handoff state
specs.value: KV bytes and metadata per transferred request
specs.context: Transfer must preserve model version, layout and request identity.

interfaces.name: Prefill pool
interfaces.signal: Completed prompt state and request deadline

interfaces.name: Decode pool
interfaces.signal: Continued token stream after verified KV handoff

lessons.tradeoff: Disaggregation can improve scheduling isolation and hardware fit, but large KV transfers or imbalanced pools can erase the gain.
lessons.whyAI: Workload phases stress compute and memory differently; useful capacity depends on serving deadlines, arrival patterns and the cost of moving state.

lessons.scale: Accelerator group to serving pool; routes schematic
mechanism: Classify the prompt work and generation work with separate latency objectives and resource estimates.
Allocate prefill and decode capacity according to the observed request mix and variability.
Transfer or expose the completed KV state with explicit ownership, layout and readiness metadata.
Admit the request to decode only when its state is accessible and scheduling deadlines remain feasible.
Measure goodput and handoff failures while varying context, batch and network load; compare with a colocated baseline.
lessons.misconception: Paged KV allocation does not itself separate prefill from decode, and phase separation is not automatically beneficial for every workload.

check.question: What new cost must a disaggregated design explicitly budget?
options: Moving or exposing KV state between phase workers
Retraining the tokenizer for each token
Eliminating all decode weights
check.explanation: The decode worker needs the prompt’s context state, making its handoff a capacity, bandwidth and correctness concern.

science.title: KV handoff floor
science.explanation: MKV is bytes actually transferred and Blink useful bytes/s on the selected path; Thandoff is seconds.
science.assumptions: A payload floor; queueing, setup, layout conversion and synchronization add latency, while reuse or shared access changes transferred bytes.

lessons.learningObjective: Judge phase separation through service objectives and state-transfer costs.
lessons.engineeringExample: Synthetic handoff: 2 GB of KV at 25 GB/s requires at least 80 ms of payload transfer. That may be acceptable for one workload and dominate another’s first-token target; a fixed universal benefit is unjustified.
lessons.evidenceNotes: DistServe and PagedAttention are distinct research methods. Their measured gains depend on workload and configurations and are not reproduced as unconditional defaults.
